<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Publish release and nightly images under the short `vllm/vllm` name, and release ROCm/XPU images under `vllm/vllm-rocm` and `vllm/vllm-xpu`, alongside the existing `vllm/vllm-openai*` repos. Each alias has the same digest as its source tag.

## Claims

- **Release** (`publish-release-images.sh`):

  | Source | Also published as |
  |---|---|
  | `vllm/vllm-openai:{latest,vX}` | `vllm/vllm:{latest,vX}` |
  | `vllm/vllm-openai:{latest,vX}-efa` | `vllm/vllm:{latest,vX}-efa` |
  | `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:{latest,vX}` | `vllm/vllm:{latest,vX}-rocm` |
  | `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:{latest,vX}-<variant>` | `vllm/vllm:{latest,vX}-<variant>` (e.g. `-rocm100`) |
  | `vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:{latest,vX}` | `vllm/vllm:{latest,vX}-cpu` |
  | `vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:{latest,vX}` | `vllm/vllm:{latest,vX}-xpu` |
  | `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:*` (all release tags, incl. `-base`) | `vllm/vllm-rocm:*` |
  | `vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:*` (all release tags, incl. `-x86_64`) | `vllm/vllm-xpu:*` |

- **Nightly** (`push-nightly-builds{,-cpu}.sh`, `xpu/push-nightly-builds-xpu.sh`, `rocm/publish.sh`): the mutable tag is also published as `vllm/vllm:nightly`, `nightly-cu134`, `nightly-cpu`, `nightly-xpu`, `nightly-rocm` and `nightly-<variant>` (e.g. `nightly-rocm100`).
- **Docs:** `docs/deployment/docker.md` gets a "Short image names" section with this mapping.

## Validation

- v0.33.0 was aliased by hand with this mapping (`crane copy`). Every alias digest matches its source, e.g. `vllm/vllm:v0.33.0` = `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.33.0` = `sha256:d825baf9ce4b…`, `vllm/vllm-rocm:v0.33.0` = `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.33.0` = `sha256:4fcd39b758b6…` (16/16 `vllm/vllm-rocm` + `vllm/vllm-xpu` tags match).
- Digest behaviour of `docker buildx imagetools create`, tested against a local `registry:2`:

  | Source | Copy keeps the digest? |
  |---|---|
  | OCI index / Docker `manifest.list.v2` (1 or 2 entries, as `docker manifest create` makes) | yes |
  | Single-arch manifest (by tag or by digest) | **no**: wrapped in a new 1-entry list |
  | One `create` call with `-t` in several repos | yes: all tags get one digest |

- Dry run of every target (`publish-release-images.sh rocm|xpu`, the four nightly scripts, `rocm/publish.sh rocm images` with `NIGHTLY=1`, `NIGHTLY=0` and `ALIAS_HUB=`) with `docker`/`aws`/`buildkite-agent` stubbed: prints exactly the tags above, and nothing under `vllm/vllm` for `NIGHTLY=0` or `ALIAS_HUB=`.
- `bash -n`, shellcheck and pre-commit pass (no new shellcheck findings).
- Not exercised in CI: these scripts only run in the release pipeline. The first nightly after merge and the v0.34.0 release are the first real runs. `vllmbot` can already push to `vllm/vllm-rocm` and `vllm/vllm-xpu` (used for the v0.33.0 copies).

## Details

- **ROCm images are single-arch**, so copying a published ROCm tag with `imagetools create` would wrap it and change its digest. The ROCm aliases (`vllm/vllm:*-rocm*`, `vllm/vllm-rocm:*`) are therefore extra `-t` flags on the `create` call that writes the canonical tags. CUDA, EFA, CPU and XPU copy a manifest list, which keeps the digest. XPU pushes the same image and list to both repos in a loop.
- **Nightly aliases are mutable tags only.** Every `vllm/vllm` nightly family shares the `nightly-` prefix, so `cleanup-nightly-builds.sh` could not prune commit tags per family, and it would delete the mutable `nightly-<suffix>` tags as well. Commit-pinned, per-arch and `base-nightly` tags stay in the canonical repos, so `vllm/vllm` needs no cleanup.
- `rocm/publish.sh` takes `ALIAS_HUB` (default `vllm/vllm`, empty to skip), like the existing `HUB` override.
- Not covered: `-rocm72` release tags (not published by this script), the EFA nightly (pending in #64028), and nightlies in `vllm/vllm-rocm` / `vllm/vllm-xpu`.
- Not a duplicate: no other open PR touches these scripts for aliasing (`gh pr list --search "publish-release-images in:files"`; #64028 only adds the EFA nightly).

@@ -21,6 +21,15 @@ target_enabled() {
   [ "${TARGET}" = "all" ] || [ "${TARGET}" = "$1" ]
 }
 
+# Mirror a published DockerHub image to vllm/vllm, the short alias of every
+# vllm/vllm-openai* repo: alias_vllm <family suffix> <src latest> <src versioned>
+# tags vllm/vllm:latest<suffix> and vllm/vllm:v<ver><suffix>. Registry-side copy,
+# so the digest is kept as long as the source is a manifest list.
+alias_vllm() {
+  docker buildx imagetools create -t "vllm/vllm:latest$1" "$2"
+  docker buildx imagetools create -t "vllm/vllm:v${RELEASE_VERSION}$1" "$3"
+}
+
 # Promote one image family from ECR staging to DockerHub: per-arch tags plus the
 # latest and versioned multi-arch manifests. $1 is the tag suffix shared by both
 # registries: "" for the default CUDA family, else e.g. "-efa".
@@ -51,6 +60,7 @@ publish_image_family() {
     "vllm/vllm-openai:v${RELEASE_VERSION}-aarch64${suffix}"
   docker manifest push "${latest}"
   docker manifest push "${versioned}"
+  alias_vllm "${suffix}" "${latest}" "${versioned}"
 }
 
 # Publish an opt-in family all-or-nothing, like the CPU images below: skip when
@@ -117,7 +127,8 @@ if target_enabled cuda-13-0-efa; then
 fi
 
 # ---- ROCm ----
-# Copied from ECR (publish.sh). The default stack (rocm) also owns the plain :latest / :v<ver> tags.
+# Copied from ECR (publish.sh) to vllm/vllm-openai-rocm and its short name vllm/vllm-rocm.
+# The default stack (rocm) also owns the plain :latest / :v<ver> tags.
 
 # pin_rocm <ref>  — <ref>@<digest>, so what was checked is what is published
 pin_rocm() {
@@ -128,7 +139,7 @@ pin_rocm() {
 }
 
 publish_rocm_stack() {
-  local v s sfx img base ver ecr=public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-release-repo:${COMMIT} hub=vllm/vllm-openai-rocm
+  local v s sfx img base ver ecr=public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-release-repo:${COMMIT} hub=vllm/vllm-openai-rocm short=vllm/vllm-rocm
   v=$(buildkite-agent meta-data get "rocm-$1-variant")
   img=$(pin_rocm "$ecr-$v")
   base=$(pin_rocm "$ecr-$v-base")
@@ -140,9 +151,14 @@ publish_rocm_stack() {
     exit 1
   fi
   sfx=("-$v"); if [[ $1 == rocm ]]; then sfx+=(""); fi
+  # One create per image tags every repo: copying the single-arch result again
+  # (alias_vllm) would wrap it in a new manifest list with a different digest.
   for s in "${sfx[@]}"; do
-    docker buildx imagetools create -t "$hub:latest$s" -t "$hub:v${RELEASE_VERSION}$s" "$img"
-    docker buildx imagetools create -t "$hub:latest$s-base" -t "$hub:v${RELEASE_VERSION}$s-base" "$base"
+    docker buildx imagetools create -t "$hub:latest$s" -t "$hub:v${RELEASE_VERSION}$s" \
+      -t "$short:latest$s" -t "$short:v${RELEASE_VERSION}$s" \
+      -t "vllm/vllm:latest${s:--rocm}" -t "vllm/vllm:v${RELEASE_VERSION}${s:--rocm}" "$img"
+    docker buildx imagetools create -t "$hub:latest$s-base" -t "$hub:v${RELEASE_VERSION}$s-base" \
+      -t "$short:latest$s-base" -t "$short:v${RELEASE_VERSION}$s-base" "$base"
   done
 }
 
@@ -153,19 +169,24 @@ fi
 # ---- XPU ----
 
 if target_enabled xpu; then
-  docker pull "public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-release-repo:${COMMIT}-x86_64-xpu"
-
-  docker tag "public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-release-repo:${COMMIT}-x86_64-xpu" vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:latest-x86_64
-  docker tag "public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-release-repo:${COMMIT}-x86_64-xpu" "vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:v${RELEASE_VERSION}-x86_64"
-  docker push vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:latest-x86_64
-  docker push "vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:v${RELEASE_VERSION}-x86_64"
-
-  docker manifest rm vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:latest || true
-  docker manifest rm "vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:v${RELEASE_VERSION}" || true
-  docker manifest create vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:latest vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:latest-x86_64 --amend
-  docker manifest create "vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:v${RELEASE_VERSION}" "vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:v${RELEASE_VERSION}-x86_64" --amend
-  docker manifest push vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:latest
-  docker manifest push "vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:v${RELEASE_VERSION}"
+  XPU_TAG=public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-release-repo:${COMMIT}-x86_64-xpu
+  docker pull "${XPU_TAG}"
+
+  # vllm/vllm-xpu is the short name of vllm/vllm-openai-xpu, with the same tags.
+  for repo in vllm/vllm-openai-xpu vllm/vllm-xpu; do
+    docker tag "${XPU_TAG}" "${repo}:latest-x86_64"
+    docker tag "${XPU_TAG}" "${repo}:v${RELEASE_VERSION}-x86_64"
+    docker push "${repo}:latest-x86_64"
+    docker push "${repo}:v${RELEASE_VERSION}-x86_64"
+
+    docker manifest rm "${repo}:latest" || true
+    docker manifest rm "${repo}:v${RELEASE_VERSION}" || true
+    docker manifest create "${repo}:latest" "${repo}:latest-x86_64" --amend
+    docker manifest create "${repo}:v${RELEASE_VERSION}" "${repo}:v${RELEASE_VERSION}-x86_64" --amend
+    docker manifest push "${repo}:latest"
+    docker manifest push "${repo}:v${RELEASE_VERSION}"
+  done
+  alias_vllm -xpu vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:latest "vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:v${RELEASE_VERSION}"
 fi
 
 # ---- CPU ----
@@ -203,6 +224,7 @@ if target_enabled cpu; then
     docker manifest create "vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:v${RELEASE_VERSION}" "vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:v${RELEASE_VERSION}-x86_64" "vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:v${RELEASE_VERSION}-arm64"
     docker manifest push vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:latest
     docker manifest push "vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:v${RELEASE_VERSION}"
+    alias_vllm -cpu vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:latest "vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:v${RELEASE_VERSION}"
   elif [ "$CPU_X86_AVAILABLE" = "false" ] && [ "$CPU_ARM_AVAILABLE" = "false" ]; then
     echo "WARNING: Neither CPU image found in ECR, skipping CPU publish (ensure block-cpu-release-image-build and block-arm64-cpu-release-image-build were unblocked and the builds finished pushing)"
   else

@@ -4,7 +4,8 @@
 #
 # Push CPU nightly images from ECR to Docker Hub as
 # vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:nightly and vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:nightly-<commit>,
-# combining the x86_64 and aarch64 architectures into a multi-arch manifest.
+# combining the x86_64 and aarch64 architectures into a multi-arch manifest,
+# and mirror :nightly to the vllm/vllm alias as vllm/vllm:nightly-cpu.
 # Run when NIGHTLY=1 after the CPU release images have been pushed to ECR.
 #
 # Local testing (no push to Docker Hub):
@@ -41,6 +42,7 @@ docker tag "$ARM64_ORIG_TAG" vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:"$TAG_NAME"-arm64
 if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "1" ]]; then
   echo "[DRY_RUN] Would push vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:$TAG_NAME-x86_64 and vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:$TAG_NAME-arm64"
   echo "[DRY_RUN] Would create and push manifests vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:$TAG_NAME and vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:$TAG_NAME_COMMIT"
+  echo "[DRY_RUN] Would mirror vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:$TAG_NAME to vllm/vllm:nightly-cpu"
   echo "[DRY_RUN] Local tags created. Exiting without push."
   exit 0
 fi
@@ -55,4 +57,7 @@ docker manifest create vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:"$TAG_NAME_COMMIT" vllm/vllm-openai-
 docker manifest push vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:"$TAG_NAME"
 docker manifest push vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:"$TAG_NAME_COMMIT"
 
-echo "Pushed vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:$TAG_NAME and vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:$TAG_NAME_COMMIT"
+# Mirror the mutable tag to the vllm/vllm alias (registry-side copy, digest kept)
+docker buildx imagetools create -t vllm/vllm:nightly-cpu vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:"$TAG_NAME"
+
+echo "Pushed vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:$TAG_NAME, vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:$TAG_NAME_COMMIT and vllm/vllm:nightly-cpu"

@@ -34,3 +34,6 @@ docker manifest create vllm/vllm-openai:"$TAG_NAME" vllm/vllm-openai:"$TAG_NAME"
 docker manifest create vllm/vllm-openai:"$TAG_NAME"-"$BUILDKITE_COMMIT" vllm/vllm-openai:"$TAG_NAME"-x86_64 vllm/vllm-openai:"$TAG_NAME"-aarch64 --amend
 docker manifest push vllm/vllm-openai:"$TAG_NAME"
 docker manifest push vllm/vllm-openai:"$TAG_NAME"-"$BUILDKITE_COMMIT"
+# mirror the mutable tag to the vllm/vllm alias, e.g. vllm/vllm:nightly or vllm/vllm:nightly-cu134
+# (registry-side copy of a manifest list, so the digest is kept)
+docker buildx imagetools create -t vllm/vllm:nightly"$ORIG_TAG_SUFFIX" vllm/vllm-openai:"$TAG_NAME"

@@ -19,6 +19,8 @@
 #
 # Optional:
 #   HUB            — Docker Hub repo for nightly images (default: vllm/vllm-openai-rocm)
+#   ALIAS_HUB      — short-name repo that also gets the mutable nightly tags as
+#                    :nightly-rocm / :nightly-<variant> (default: vllm/vllm; empty to skip)
 #   NIGHTLY        — set to 1 to push nightly Hub tags (default: 0)
 #   DOCKERHUB_USERNAME — Hub username for cleanup script (default: vllmbot)
 set -euo pipefail
@@ -33,6 +35,7 @@ COMMIT=${BUILDKITE_COMMIT:?BUILDKITE_COMMIT must be set}

 HUB=${HUB:-vllm/vllm-openai-rocm}
+ALIAS_HUB=${ALIAS_HUB-vllm/vllm}
 
 # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 # Helper functions
@@ -166,13 +169,20 @@ EOF

     [[ $STACK == rocm ]] && suffixes+=("")
 
+    # $ALIAS_HUB gets only the mutable tag: its families share the nightly-
+    # prefix, so the commit tags could not be pruned per family. It is tagged in
+    # the same create, as re-copying a single-arch image changes its digest.
     hub_tags=""
     for sfx in "${suffixes[@]}"; do
-      docker buildx imagetools create \
-        -t "$HUB:nightly$sfx" -t "$HUB:nightly$sfx-$COMMIT" "$IMG"
+      tags=(-t "$HUB:nightly$sfx" -t "$HUB:nightly$sfx-$COMMIT")
+      hub_tags="$hub_tags \`$HUB:nightly$sfx\` \`$HUB:nightly$sfx-$COMMIT\`"
+      if [[ -n $ALIAS_HUB ]]; then
+        tags+=(-t "$ALIAS_HUB:nightly${sfx:--rocm}")
+        hub_tags="$hub_tags \`$ALIAS_HUB:nightly${sfx:--rocm}\`"
+      fi
+      docker buildx imagetools create "${tags[@]}" "$IMG"
       docker buildx imagetools create \
         -t "$HUB:base-nightly$sfx" -t "$HUB:base-nightly$sfx-$COMMIT" "$RT"
-      hub_tags="$hub_tags \`$HUB:nightly$sfx\` \`$HUB:nightly$sfx-$COMMIT\`"
     done
 
     # Prune old nightly tags (keep last 14 builds per tag family).

@@ -18,4 +18,7 @@ docker manifest rm ${REPO}:nightly-"$BUILDKITE_COMMIT" || true
 docker manifest create ${REPO}:nightly ${REPO}:nightly-x86_64 --amend
 docker manifest create ${REPO}:nightly-"$BUILDKITE_COMMIT" ${REPO}:nightly-x86_64 --amend
 docker manifest push ${REPO}:nightly

+### Short image names
+
+Release images (from v0.33.0) and nightly images are also published under the
+shorter `vllm/vllm` name, with the platform as a tag suffix. These are the same
+images (same digests) as the `vllm/vllm-openai*` tags.
+
+| Image | `vllm/vllm` tag |
+| --- | --- |
+| `vllm/vllm-openai:{latest,v<version>,nightly}` | `vllm/vllm:{latest,v<version>,nightly}` |
+| `vllm/vllm-openai:{latest,v<version>}-efa` | `vllm/vllm:{latest,v<version>}-efa` |
+| `vllm/vllm-openai:cu134-nightly` | `vllm/vllm:nightly-cu134` |
+| `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:{latest,v<version>,nightly}` | `vllm/vllm:{latest,v<version>,nightly}-rocm` |
+| `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:{latest,v<version>,nightly}-<variant>` | `vllm/vllm:{latest,v<version>,nightly}-<variant>`, e.g. `-rocm100` |
+| `vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:{latest,v<version>,nightly}` | `vllm/vllm:{latest,v<version>,nightly}-cpu` |
+| `vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:{latest,v<version>,nightly}` | `vllm/vllm:{latest,v<version>,nightly}-xpu` |
+
+For example, `docker pull vllm/vllm:v0.33.0-rocm` pulls the same image as
+`docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.33.0`. Per-architecture tags, ROCm `-base`
+images and commit-pinned nightly tags (`nightly-<commit>`) are only published
+under the `vllm/vllm-openai*` names.
+
+Release images for ROCm and XPU are also published as `vllm/vllm-rocm` and
+`vllm/vllm-xpu`, with the same tags as `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm` and
+`vllm/vllm-openai-xpu` (e.g. `vllm/vllm-rocm:v0.33.0`, `vllm/vllm-xpu:latest`).
+
